entities.name: Alfonso I of Asturias
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Alfonso I of Asturias, called the Catholic, was the third king of Asturias, reigning from 739 to his death in 757. His reign saw a great extension of the Christian domain of Asturias, reconquering Galicia and León.

As the leader of the Asturian kingdom, Alfonso I played a crucial role in the Reconquista, a centuries-long process of Christian reconquest of the Iberian Peninsula from Muslim rule. His military campaigns, supported by the Visigoths and other Christian kingdoms, led to the recapture of key cities and territories, paving the way for the eventual unification of the peninsula under Christian rule.

Alfonso I's reign also saw significant cultural and artistic developments, including the establishment of the Asturian court, which attracted scholars and artists from across the Mediterranean. The king himself was a patron of learning and a supporter of the Christian church, and his court became a center of learning and culture that rivalled those of the Byzantine Empire and the Abbasid Caliphate.

Despite his significant achievements, Alfonso I's legacy has been somewhat overshadowed by that of his successors, who went on to build the Kingdom of Castile and other powerful Christian states in the Iberian Peninsula.

"As for our kingdom, we are the most powerful and the most Christian in all of the world," Alfonso I declared in a speech to his nobles in 755, "and we will not be defeated by the infidels, for God is on our side." These words would prove prophetic, as Alfonso I's military campaigns would ultimately lead to the Christian reconquest of the Iberian Peninsula and the establishment of a Christian kingdom that would endure for centuries.
